To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) alpha-tocopherols can reduce oxidative degradation and improve the wear properties of UHMWPE, (ii) alpha-tocopheryl-blended UHMWPE can be cross-linked by gamma irradiation, but to a lesser degree than virgin UHMW-PE, and (iii) the mechanical properties of alpha-tocophery-blended UHMWPES can be improved by gamma irradiation.
the addition of alpha-tocophenol to UHMWPE before irradiation reduced the oxidative degradation and wear of the irradiated polymer.
the incorporation of alpha-tocopheryl acetate into UHMW polyethylene prior to gamma irradiation can improve the wear resistance of UHMWPE in an accelerated aging environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing radiation cross-linked ultra-high molecular weight PE (UHMW-PE) for biomedical applications.
the characterization of the effect of alpha tocopherol-blended UHMWPE on crosslinking efficiency, wear behavior, and mechanical properties of UHMWPE.
the characterization of irradiated blends containing alpha-tocopherols and UHMW-PE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of alpha-tocpherol to UHMWPE before consolidation and irradiation results in an improvement in wear resistance and oxidative stability of the UHMWPE, but at the expense of a reduction in its mechanical properties and cross-link density.
100-kG-y irradiated UHMWP-E previously blended with 10 wt% alpha-topherol is superior to 100-kGY irradiated virgin UHMW-PE in terms of oxidative stability, wear resistance, and mechanical properties.

the addition of alpha-tocoperol to UHMWPE before consolidation and gamma-irradiation reduces the oxidative degradation of the irradiated UHMWPPE and improves its mechanical properties, while maintaining its wear resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

alpha-tocpherol blended UHMWPE resins can be cross-linked by gamma-irradiation to the same extent and have the same wear properties as the unblended UHMWPE, but with the advantage of increased oxidation stability.

alpha-tocpherol-blended 0.1 wt% 100-kGry irradiated UHMWPPEs were more stable to oxidation, had better wear resistance, and better mechanical properties when compared to 0.3% alpha-tocpherole-blended 100-ky irradiated UHMWEPE.
the addition of alpha-tocopheryl to UHMWPE, prior to irradiation, is a viable alternative to post- irradiation melting.
The main takeaway from our work is that

blending UHMWPE with alpha-tocopheryl acetate prior to consolidation and irradiation is a promising strategy for reducing oxidative degradation of UHMWPE without sacrificing wear and mechanical properties.
the presence of alpha-tocpherol during gamma irradiation of UHMWPE inhibits cross-linking.
alpha-tocoberol blended UHMWPE is more resistant to oxidation and wear than virgin UHMW PE, and it also exhibits improved mechanical properties after irradiation.
